evidence_items.locator: Table 2.9 Quarterly operating leverage (columns: revenue $bn, expenses $bn, expenses % revenue, revenue change, expense change, incremental margin %)
evidence_items.explanation: In every 2025 quarter, operating expenses rose by at least as much as revenue (negative incremental margins) and stayed at 2 to 3.5 times revenue. This fits the 'costs scale with revenue' part of the claim for last year.

evidence_items.locator: Table 2.9 Quarterly operating leverage, Q4 2025 to Q2 2026 rows
evidence_items.explanation: The break from the 2025 pattern began in Q1 2026, not Q2. Revenue rose 132% that quarter while expenses rose 31%, and expenses fell from 239% to 135% of revenue. In Q2, expenses still rose 65%, by $4.18bn.

derived.formula: Growth = later / earlier - 1. Revenue Q4 2025 to Q1 2026: 4.73/2.04 - 1. Expenses Q4 2025 to Q1 2026: 6.40/4.88 - 1. Expenses Q1 to Q2 2026: 10.58/6.40 - 1.
derived.rounding: Nearest whole percent: revenue +132%, expenses +31% (Q1 2026); expenses +65% (Q2 2026)

evidence_items.locator: Citation of S-1 page 158, quarterly statements as a percentage of revenue
evidence_items.explanation: Compute and infrastructure fell from 144% of revenue in Q4 2025 to 72% in Q1 2026, a bigger drop than the later fall to 48% in Q2. Compute had already stopped keeping pace with revenue before the second quarter.

metric_scope.metric: Compute and infrastructure expense as % of revenue, quarterly

receipt.public_excerpt: Q2 2026 is the first profitable quarter: operating income of $1.0B, an 8% operating margin, and adjusted operating income of $2.2B at a 19% adjusted margin.

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms that Q2 2026 was the first quarter with an operating profit. The 'Q2 was different' part of the claim is accurate as far as profit goes.

unresolved_gaps: The WSJ chart the speaker described is paywalled and could not be inspected. It may have shown only some quarters or different series, which would bear on how reasonable his reading of it was.
